primary.title: Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji)
primary.author: Sima Qian
primary.rationale: While not authored by Qin Shi Huang himself, the Shiji is the most important and earliest comprehensive historical account of his reign and life, compiled by a historian who had access to earlier records and oral traditions. It contains decrees and speeches attributed to Qin Shi Huang.

secondary.title: The Cambridge History of Ancient China: From the Origins of Civilization to 221 BC
secondary.author: Michael Loewe and Edward L. Shaughnessy
secondary.rationale: This is a comprehensive and authoritative academic work covering the period leading up to and including the Qin dynasty. It features scholarly chapters on Qin Shi Huang and his era.

secondary.title: The First Emperor: China's Terracotta Army
secondary.author: Jane Portal
secondary.rationale: This book, often accompanying major exhibitions, provides a scholarly overview of Qin Shi Huang's reign, his achievements, and the context of the Terracotta Army, drawing on archaeological and historical research.

secondary.title: Qin Shi Huang: The First Emperor of China
secondary.author: Li Yu
secondary.rationale: A scholarly biography focusing on Qin Shi Huang, synthesizing historical evidence and archaeological findings to present a detailed account of his life and impact.

suggestions.notes: Direct primary sources authored by Qin Shi Huang are extremely rare and typically exist only as fragments or inscriptions recorded in later historical texts. The 'Records of the Grand Historian' is the closest available primary source that provides extensive information attributed to him.
